# hyperlite_network (Resource)

A virtual network of the node: NAT or isolated with Hyperlite's DHCP, or a bridge onto a host bridge.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hyperlite_network" "lan" {
  name       = "lan"
  mode       = "nat"
  address    = "10.0.20.1"
  dhcp_start = "10.0.20.100"
  dhcp_end   = "10.0.20.200"
}

resource "hyperlite_network" "dmz" {
  name   = "dmz"
  mode   = "bridge"
  bridge = "br0"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) `nat` (routed to the host's network), `isolated` (no way out) or `bridge` (onto a host bridge). Between `nat` and `isolated` it changes in place; to or from `bridge`, the network is replaced.
- `name` (String) Its name. A change renames it.

### Optional

- `address` (String) For `nat` and `isolated`: the gateway's address (`10.0.20.1`).
- `autostart` (Boolean) Started with the node.
- `bridge` (String) For `bridge`: the host bridge (`br0`).
- `dhcp_end` (String) Last address of the DHCP range.
- `dhcp_start` (String) First address Hyperlite's DHCP hands out (with `dhcp_end`; none: no DHCP).
- `netmask` (String) Its netmask (`255.255.255.0` when absent).
- `node` (String) The member of the cluster the network is on (absent: the node the provider talks to). Another member makes it again there.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Started.
- `id` (String) The network's name.
- `uuid` (String) Its libvirt UUID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the network's name; the same led by `<node>/` for one on another node of the cluster.
terraform import hyperlite_network.lan lan
terraform import hyperlite_network.lan pve-b/lan
```
